### 📄 PAGE 2: Fundamental Principles & Theory Deep-Dive

---

#### [BLUE] 📘 THE EVOLUTION AND NATURE OF HTML
*   **Definition:** **HTML** stands for **HyperText Markup Language**. It is the standard markup language used to create documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
*   **HyperText:** Refers to text that contains links (*hyperlinks*) to other texts, allowing non-linear navigation of digital information.
*   **Markup Language:** A system for annotating a document in a way that is syntactically distinguishable from the text, instructing the browser on how to structure, format, and present the content.
*   **Inventor:** Developed by **Tim Berners-Lee** at CERN in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
*   **Role in Web Ecosystem:** Acts as the skeleton or structural blueprint of a webpage, upon which CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) adds design and JavaScript adds behavior.

---

#### [GOLD] ⚙️ HOW WEB BROWSERS INTERPRET MARKUP
*   **Client-Side Rendering:** The web browser acts as the client interpreter. It reads the raw HTML source code line by line from top to bottom.
*   **Tag Suppression:** The browser **does not display** the HTML tags themselves; instead, it uses them as instructions to render the enclosed content visually.
*   **Rendering Engine:** Modern browsers use sophisticated rendering engines (e.g., Blink, Gecko, WebKit) to transform raw text markup into the graphical User Interface (UI) seen by users.

---

#### [RED] 🔍 DISTINCTION: MARKUP VS. PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES
*   **Not a Programming Language:** HTML lacks variables, loops, conditional logic (if/else statements), and arithmetic calculation capabilities. Therefore, it is strictly classified as a *markup language*.
*   **Deterministic Output:** Given the same HTML code, every compliant browser will parse and display the foundational structural elements identically.

---

#### [GREEN] 🛠️ ESSENTIAL TOOLS FOR HTML DEVELOPMENT
*   **Text Editor (The Authoring Tool):** A basic ASCII or plain text editor used to write and edit code.
    *   *Examples:* Notepad (Windows), TextEdit (macOS), Notepad++, VS Code.
    *   *DAV Note:* Never use Microsoft Word or rich-text processors for writing code, as they inject hidden formatting metadata (`.docx` formatting codes) that corrupts HTML execution.
*   **Web Browser (The Rendering Tool):** An application used to view and test web pages.
    *   *Examples:* Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Safari.

# 🌐 THE DAV DICTIONARY — ACADEMIC NOTES AUTHOR ## CLASS: 8 | SUBJECT: HANDS ON COMPUTER / ICT | CHAPTER 2: HTML-I ### 📄 PAGE 3: Scientific Laws, Formulas, Equations & Principles --- #### [BLUE] 📐 THE CORE PRINCIPLE OF TAG ENCLOSURE * **Principle of Nesting (The Russian Doll Rule):** When multiple tags are opened within one another, they **must** be closed in the exact reverse order of their opening. * *Mathematical Representation:* If opening sequence is $\text{Tag}_A \rightarrow \text{Tag}_B$, the closing sequence must be $\text{Tag}_B \rightarrow \text{Tag}_A$. * *Valid Syntax:* `DAV Public School` * *Invalid Syntax:* `DAV Public School` (Cross-nesting causes parser errors and unpredictable rendering). --- #### [GOLD] 🧬 THE ANATOMY OF AN HTML ELEMENT * **General Formula of an Element:** $$\text{Element} = \text{Opening Tag} + \text{Content} + \text{Closing Tag}$$ * **Component Breakdown:** * **Opening Tag:** Consists of a keyword enclosed in angle brackets, e.g., `

`. * **Content:** The raw data, text, or nested elements placed between the tags. * **Closing Tag:** Consists of the same keyword preceded by a forward slash (`/`) enclosed in angle brackets, e.g., `

`. --- #### [RED] ⚖️ THE TWO-FOLD CLASSIFICATION OF ELEMENTS * **Container Elements (Paired Tags):** Elements that require both an opening and a closing tag to enclose content. * *Formula:* `Content goes here` * *Examples:* ``, `<p>`, `<b>`, `<h1>` * **Empty Elements (Unpaired Tags / Singleton Tags):** Elements that perform a specific function and do not take any content or require a closing tag. * *Formula:* `<tag>` (or optionally `<tag />` in XHTML). * *Examples:* `<br>` (Line Break), `<hr>` (Horizontal Rule). --- #### [GREEN] 📜 THE BASIC HTML DOCUMENT SKELETON (THE "GOLDEN TEMPLATE") * Every standard DAV-approved HTML document follows this exact structural blueprint: ```html <!DOCTYPE html> <html> <head> <title>Page Title Goes Here ```

# 🌐 THE DAV DICTIONARY — ACADEMIC NOTES AUTHOR ## CLASS: 8 | SUBJECT: HANDS ON COMPUTER / ICT | CHAPTER 2: HTML-I ### 📄 PAGE 4: Exhaustive Technical Glossary & Precision Definitions --- #### [BLUE] 🔤 TERMINOLOGY & DEFINITIONS (A - H) * **Attribute:** A modifier used to decorate or modify the behavior of an HTML element, always specified inside the opening tag (e.g., `align="center"`). * **Browser:** A software application used to locate, retrieve, and display content on the World Wide Web. * **Container Element:** An HTML tag that encloses text or other elements and requires a closing tag containing a forward slash (`/`). * **Document Type Declaration (``):** An instruction to the web browser about what version of HTML the document is written in (specifically HTML5). * **Empty Element:** A standalone HTML tag that performs an action without enclosing content and does not require a closing tag. * **Heading Tag (`

` to `

`):** Semantic elements used to define document headings, where `

` represents the highest level and `

` the lowest. * **HTML:** HyperText Markup Language; the foundational language used to structure web pages. --- #### [GOLD] 🔤 TERMINOLOGY & DEFINITIONS (I - Z) * **Markup Language:** A computer language that uses tags to define elements within a document, separating structure from plain text. * **Nesting:** The practice of placing one HTML element inside another element. * **Paragraph Tag (`

`):** A container element used to group blocks of text into distinct paragraphs. * **Source Code:** The underlying human-readable text file written in HTML that browsers compile and render into graphical pages. * **Tag:** A markup construct starting with `<` and ending with `>`, serving as the fundamental building block of HTML. * **Web Page:** A digital document written in HTML, accessible via the internet or local storage through a web browser. * **Whitespace:** Spaces, tabs, and newline characters in source code; HTML collapses multiple consecutive whitespaces into a single space on the rendered page. --- #### [RED] ⚠️ CRITICAL DISTINCTION BOX: SOURCE CODE VS. RENDERED OUTPUT * **Source Code:** What the developer types in the text editor (e.g., `Bold Text`). * **Rendered Output:** What the user sees on the screen after the browser parses the code (**Bold Text**).

# 🌐 THE DAV DICTIONARY — ACADEMIC NOTES AUTHOR ## CLASS: 8 | SUBJECT: HANDS ON COMPUTER / ICT | CHAPTER 2: HTML-I ### 📄 PAGE 5: Detailed Page-by-Page Textbook Highlights & Core Factoids --- #### [BLUE] 📖 THE ANATOMY OF THE `` AND `` SECTIONS * **The `` Section:** * Acts as the administrative container of the document. * Contains metadata, scripts, and the document title. * Content placed inside the `` tag **is not** displayed directly in the main browser viewport. * **The `` Tag:** * Must always be nested inside the `<head>` section. * Defines the text displayed on the browser tab or window title bar. * **The `<body>` Section:** * Acts as the primary display container for all visible webpage content. * All text, images, links, tables, and multimedia elements **must** be placed inside the `<body>...</body>` block to be seen by users. --- #### [GOLD] 📖 STRUCTURAL AND TEXT FORMATTING HIGHLIGHTS * **Paragraph Management (`<p>`):** Automatically adds a vertical blank space (margin) before and after the enclosed block of text. * **Line Break (`<br>`):** Inserts a single carriage return (line break) without starting a new paragraph. It is an empty element. * **Horizontal Rule (`<hr>`):** Draws a horizontal divider line across the width of the webpage to separate sections visually. It is an empty element. * **Physical Text Formatting Tags:** * `<b>...</b>`: Renders text in **Bold**. * `<i>...</i>`: Renders text in *Italic*. * `<u>...</u>`: Renders text with an <u>Underline</u>. --- #### [RED] 📖 HEADING HIERARCHY RULES * HTML provides six levels of headings: `<h1>`, `<h2>`, `<h3>`, `<h4>`, `<h5>`, and `<h6>`. * **Size Scalability:** `<h1>` renders the largest and boldest heading; `<h6>` renders the smallest. * **Semantic Importance:** Search engines and screen readers use heading tags to index the structural hierarchy of a document. Skipping levels (e.g., jumping from `<h1>` directly to `<h4>`) is considered poor coding practice.

# 🌐 THE DAV DICTIONARY — ACADEMIC NOTES AUTHOR ## CLASS: 8 | SUBJECT: HANDS ON COMPUTER / ICT | CHAPTER 2: HTML-I ### 📄 PAGE 6: Conceptual Breakdown, Practical Examples & Applications --- #### [BLUE] 💻 COMPLETE PRACTICAL EXAMPLE: A DAV SCHOOL WEBPAGE * Study this complete, clean, and valid HTML source code file demonstrating foundational tags: ```html DAV Public School - Web Portal

Welcome to DAV ICT Education

HTML is the standard markup language for creating web pages.

It was created by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN.


Key Formatting Tags:

This text is normal, but this text is italicized, and this text is underlined.

``` --- #### [GOLD] 🔍 LINE-BY-LINE CODE EXECUTION ANALYSIS * ``: Declares document type as HTML5. * ``: Root wrapper establishing the document boundary. * `` & ``: Sets the browser tab title to "DAV Public School - Web Portal". * `<h1>...</h1>`: Displays a prominent main heading. * `<hr>`: Draws a horizontal dividing line across the page width. * `<p>...<b>...</b>...</p>`: Renders a paragraph containing bold-formatted keywords. * `<br>`: Forces a clean vertical line break before the subheading. --- #### [RED] ⚠️ COMMON SYNTAX PITFALLS TO AVOID * **Unclosed Tags:** Forgetting to close a container tag (e.g., writing `<b>DAV` without `</b>`) causes all subsequent text on the page to remain bold. * **Wrong Slash Direction:** Using a backward slash (`\`) instead of a forward slash (`/`) in closing tags (e.g., `<p>Text<\p>`) will cause the browser to ignore the close instruction and render errors. * **Missing File Extension:** Saving a file as `index` instead of `index.html` prevents the browser from identifying it as a webpage.

# 🌐 THE DAV DICTIONARY — ACADEMIC NOTES AUTHOR ## CLASS: 8 | SUBJECT: HANDS ON COMPUTER / ICT | CHAPTER 2: HTML-I ### 📄 PAGE 10: 5-Minute Rapid Exam Booster Summary & Memory Anchors --- #### [BLUE] 🚀 60-SECOND RAPID REVISION BULLETS * **HTML Definition:** HyperText Markup Language, invented by Tim Berners-Lee, used to build webpage structures. * **File Extension:** Always save with `.html` or `.htm`. * **Root Structure:** ``, ``, ``, and `<body>`. * **Container Tags:** Require both opening and closing tags (e.g., `<p>`, `<b>`, `<h1>`). * **Empty Tags:** Standalone tags requiring no closing tag (e.g., `<br>`, `<hr>`). * **Headings:** Ranging from `<h1>` (largest) to `<h6>` (smallest). * **Whitespace Rule:** HTML collapses consecutive spaces and line breaks into a single space; use `<br>` for forced line breaks. --- #### [GOLD] ⚓ MEMORY ANCHORS & ACRONYMS * **H-T-M-L:** **H**yper**T**ext **M**arkup **L**anguage — *Structure of the Web!* * **The Sandwich Rule for Nesting:** *Inside tags must be closed before outside tags!* (Bottom bun `<b>`, filling `Text`, top bun `</b>`). --- #### [RED] ⚡ FINAL DAV BOARD EXAM CHECKLIST * [ ] Did you include `<!DOCTYPE html>` at the very top? * [ ] Are all container tags properly closed with a forward slash (`/`)? * [ ] Is the `<title>` nested strictly inside the `<head>` section? * [ ] Is all visible text placed inside the `<body>` section? * [ ] Are you saving the file with the correct `.html` extension? --- *End of Chapter 2 Master Study Notes — Class 8 ICT (DAV Dictionary)*
